en.documentTitle: Broken Beach (Pasih Uug), Nusa Penida: Name, Meaning & Landscape
en.metaDescription: Why Broken Beach is also called Pasih Uug, what the local name means, and how the coastal arch and cove formed in Nusa Penida, Bali.
en.title: Broken Beach and Pasih Uug: one place, two names
en.lead: Broken Beach and Pasih Uug refer to the same coastal feature on Nusa Penida. Understanding both names helps you read maps, local signs and travel posts without confusion.

blocks.heading: What the names mean
paragraphs: Broken Beach is the English label most visitors and mapping services use for the natural arch on Nusa Penida's west coast. Pasih Uug is the local Balinese name for the same spot; Pasih means sea or beach and Uug means broken or damaged, which matches the open arch in the rock.

blocks.heading: Why two names appear together
paragraphs: Government tourism pages for Klungkung and Nusa Penida publish Pasih Uug and Broken Beach side by side, and a 2020 district post retells a local formation legend. Use whichever name your map shows; they point to the same coastal opening.

blocks.heading: A note on spelling and labels
paragraphs: You may see Pasih Uug, Pasih Uug Beach or Pantai Pasih Uug. Map labels and village descriptions differ, and the pin sits in Sakti while some regency reports mention Bunga Mekar. Treat the pin as a location reference, not a verified entrance or village boundary.

faqs: Is Broken Beach the same as Pasih Uug?
Yes. They describe the same natural coastal arch and cove on Nusa Penida. Pasih Uug is the local name, Broken Beach the common English label.
What does Pasih Uug mean?
In local usage Pasih Uug is read as broken sea or broken beach, describing the rock opening carved to the sea. It is a place name, not an official safety rating.
Is it the same as Angel's Billabong?
No. Angel's Billabong is a separate coastal pool formation nearby. Its access and water rules are different and must be checked on their own.

blocks.heading: Which harbour for the west coast

Allow buffer time for rough roads and swell.

en.documentTitle: Kelingking Beach to Broken Beach: Route & Drive
en.metaDescription: How to travel between Kelingking Beach and Broken Beach on Nusa Penida, including road distance and how to link them in one day.

blocks.heading: Where Kelingking is

blocks.heading: Linking the two
paragraphs: Most visitors join them with a west-coast loop that also includes Angel's Billabong, Paluang Cliff and sometimes Crystal Bay. A private car with driver makes the connection far easier than multiple scooter trips.

Should I visit both in one day?
Yes, they are usually combined in a west-coast loop with Angel's Billabong and Paluang Cliff.

blocks.heading: Where Crystal Bay is

blocks.heading: Combining the two

blocks.heading: Order and timing

Crystal Bay is a swimming spot; Broken Beach is a viewpoint only.
Confirm sea conditions before entering the water anywhere.

faqs: How far is Broken Beach from Crystal Bay?
Roughly 45 to 70 minutes by road, because Crystal Bay is on the north-west coast.
Can I swim at Crystal Bay and view Broken Beach the same day?
Yes, they are often combined in a west-coast loop; Crystal Bay for swimming, Broken Beach for the viewpoint.

en.documentTitle: Nusa Penida Transport: Private Car with Driver vs Scooter
en.metaDescription: Choosing between hiring a car with driver or riding a scooter on Nusa Penida, with road-condition and safety notes for reaching Broken Beach.
en.title: Car with driver or scooter?
en.lead: Most visitors reach Broken Beach by private car with driver or by rented scooter. The choice affects comfort, safety on rough roads and how easily you link several stops.

blocks.heading: Private car with driver
paragraphs: A car with driver is the easier option for the island's rough roads, especially if you plan several west-coast stops in one day. The driver handles navigation and parking while you focus on the views.

blocks.heading: Scooter rental
paragraphs: A scooter gives flexibility and lower cost, but Nusa Penida roads are rough, hilly and often dusty. Only ride if you are confident on similar terrain, wear a helmet, and avoid it in bad weather.

blocks.heading: Other options
paragraphs: Shared tours and arranged transfers also exist. Whatever you choose, confirm the meeting point, destination and return plan before you sail.
bullets: Car with driver suits groups, families and rough-road days.
Scooter suits confident riders in dry conditions.
Confirm price, duration and what is included before paying.

faqs: Is a driver worth it on Nusa Penida?
For the rough west-coast roads and multiple stops, a car with driver is usually the easier and safer choice.
Can I ride a scooter to Broken Beach?
Yes, but only if you are confident on rough, hilly roads. Wear a helmet and avoid scooters in bad weather.
What should I confirm before paying?
Agree the price, duration, pickup point, destination and return plan with the provider.

blocks.heading: Mobil pribadi dengan supir
paragraphs: Mobil dengan supir adalah opsi lebih mudah untuk jalan pulau yang kasar, terutama bila merencanakan beberapa pemberhentian pesisir barat dalam sehari. Supir menangani navigasi dan parkir sementara Anda fokus pada pemandangan.

paragraphs: Sepeda motor memberi fleksibilitas dan biaya lebih rendah, namun jalan Nusa Penida kasar, berbukit, dan sering berdebu. Hanya mengendarai jika Anda yakin di medan serupa, kenakan helm, dan hindari saat cuaca buruk.

faqs: Apakah supir sepadan di Nusa Penida?

Sepakati harga, durasi, titik jemput, tujuan, dan rencana kembali dengan penyedia.

en.documentTitle: Nusa Penida Roads: Conditions & Driving Safety
en.metaDescription: What to expect from Nusa Penida's roads on the way to Broken Beach, and safety tips for drivers and scooter riders.
en.title: Roads and driving safety
en.lead: Nusa Penida's roads are noticeably rougher than mainland Bali. The drive to Broken Beach crosses uneven, hilly terrain, so plan for slow sections rather than fast miles.

blocks.heading: What the roads are like
paragraphs: Expect potholes, loose gravel, steep dips and narrow passes in places. After rain, sections can become muddy or slippery, and afternoon dust is common in dry weather.

blocks.heading: Safety tips
paragraphs: Drive slowly, keep a safe distance, and avoid the scooter option entirely in heavy rain or on unfamiliar rough stretches. A local driver who knows the conditions is a real advantage.

blocks.heading: Plan with buffer
paragraphs: Because travel times depend on road state, treat published minute estimates as rough guides and add buffer so one delay does not ruin the day.
bullets: Lower your speed on rough and hilly sections.
Wear a helmet if on a scooter.
Avoid night driving where possible.
Keep cash for any small roadside needs.

faqs: Are the roads to Broken Beach paved?
Parts are paved but rough, with potholes, gravel and steep dips in places. Expect a slow, bumpy drive.
Is it safe to ride a scooter?
Only for confident riders in good conditions. Avoid scooters in rain or on rough unfamiliar stretches.
How long does the drive really take?
Treat estimates as rough; conditions, not distance, set the time. Add buffer for delays.

id.documentTitle: Jalan Nusa Penida: Kondisi & Keselamatan Berkendara
id.metaDescription: Apa yang diharapkan dari jalan Nusa Penida menuju Broken Beach, dan tips keselamatan untuk pengemudi dan pengendara sepeda motor.
id.title: Jalan dan keselamatan berkendara
id.lead: Jalan Nusa Penida jauh lebih kasar daripada Bali daratan. Perjalanan ke Broken Beach melintasi medan tidak rata dan berbukit, jadi rencanakan bagian lambat daripada kecepatan tinggi.

blocks.heading: Seperti apa jalannya
paragraphs: Harapkan lubang, kerikil lepas, turunan curam, dan jalan sempit di beberapa tempat. Setelah hujan, bagian dapat berlumpur atau licin, dan debu sore umum di cuaca kering.

blocks.heading: Tips keselamatan
paragraphs: Berkendaralah perlahan, jaga jarak aman, dan hindari sepeda motor sama sekali saat hujan lebat atau di ruas kasar tak dikenal. Supir lokal yang tahu kondisi adalah keuntungan nyata.

faqs: Apakah jalan ke Broken Beach beraspal?
Sebagian beraspal namun kasar, dengan lubang, kerikil, dan turunan curam di tempat. Harapkan perjalanan lambat dan berguncang.
Apakah aman naik sepeda motor?
Hanya untuk pengendara yakin dalam kondisi baik. Hindari sepeda motor saat hujan atau di ruas kasar tak dikenal.
Berapa lama perjalanan sebenarnya?
Anggap estimasi kasar; kondisi, bukan jarak, yang menentukan waktu. Tambahkan waktu tambahan untuk keterlambatan.

blocks.heading: How it differs from Broken Beach
paragraphs: Broken Beach is a cliff-top viewpoint over a cove; Angel's Billabong is a sea pool at a lower level. The two are close but their access and safety rules are not the same.

Confirm access and rules on the day.

Sekitar 30 sampai 50 menit dengan jalan pulau yang kasar.
